A PDF can now be deflated by an encoder the host brings, and the command line, the native library and the preview
server offer Zopfli: the same document, 6 to 12 per cent smaller. Every PDF is also 1,980 bytes lighter, and asking a
backend for its document twice no longer writes it twice over.

**Documents change in one way unless you ask for more**: the XMP packet carries no padding, so every PDF is 1,980 bytes
smaller and nothing on the page moves. Zopfli changes nothing until it is asked for. A delegate, two properties and new
options are added, and a backend that has assembled its document now refuses a page drawn after it, hence 0.12 rather
than 0.11.1.

## New: a smaller file, with an encoder you bring

The engine still deflates with the framework's zlib and depends on nothing new. A host that wants a smaller file hands
`PdfBackend` another encoder - here Zopfli, through the [ZopfliSharp](https://www.nuget.org/packages/ZopfliSharp)
package:

```csharp
pdf.Compressor = data => Zopfli.Compress(data, ZopfliFormat.Zlib);
```

- **Every stream the file deflates goes through it**: pages, fonts, pictures, object streams and the cross-reference
  stream. An opaque PNG, whose data used to go in as it came, has its rows inflated and deflated again behind the same
  predictor, so no pixel changes; on an invoice whose weight is its logo, that is most of the gain. A JPEG, the XMP packet
  and the streams of a page imported from another PDF go in as they came.
- **What it hands back is checked before it goes in.** Each answer is inflated and compared with what it was given, and
  one that is not a zlib stream of those bytes is refused, naming the fault. `ZopfliFormat.Deflate` in place of
  `ZopfliFormat.Zlib` would otherwise give a page a reader draws blank.
- **`CompressionThreads`** deflates several streams at once, for the same bytes. It is 1 by default, since a library
  takes no threads its caller did not offer; -1 takes the machine.

Measured on eight cores:

| | zlib | Zopfli | smaller by | Zopfli, one thread | Zopfli, every core |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| the ACME invoice | 52,146 bytes | 48,712 bytes | 6.6% | 5.0 s | 1.5 s |
| the showcase, PDF/A-3B and tagged | 105,591 bytes | 93,262 bytes | 11.7% | 26 s | 9.4 s |

zlib takes a few hundredths of a second for either, so Zopfli is for a file written once and kept or sent many times -
an archive, a batch - and not for one somebody is waiting on. It writes the same bytes on Windows and Linux, which zlib
does not. The documents pass veraPDF on PDF/A-3B and PDF/UA-1 either way.

## New: Zopfli in the command line, the native library and the preview server

| | How to ask | Passes over each stream | Threads |
|---|---|---|---|
| `frisket render` | `--zopfli` | `--zopfli-iterations <n>` | every core |
| `fk_render` | `"compression": "zopfli"` | `"iterations": n` | `"threads"`: 1 by default, -1 for every core |
| `POST /pdf` | `"compression": "zopfli"` | `"iterations": n` | one |

Passes are refused without Zopfli, and so is a compression none of them knows. Through the native library the render's
token reaches Zopfli too, so a cancellation lands between two passes and comes back `FK_CANCELLED`. The C++ and Pascal
wrappers have `zopfli`, `zopfli_iterations` and `compression_threads`; the Python one passes `compression="zopfli"` like
any other option. The server never uses Zopfli unless a request asks.

## Fixed: a second `ToArray` wrote the document twice over

Each call to `ToArray` assembled the whole document again after what the previous call had written, and the file named
only the newest copy. A `Save` followed by a `ToArray` - one copy kept, one sent - sent a file twice as heavy, valid, and
nothing said so. The document is now assembled once, and every call hands back the same bytes, as a copy of its own.

## Fixed: two kilobytes of spaces in every PDF

XMP's convention ends a packet with 2 KB of padding so a tool can rewrite it in place. In a PDF that would put the
information dictionary out of step with the packet, which PDF/A refuses, and break a signature over those bytes. The
padding is gone; the packet stays uncompressed and readable.

## Worth checking

- **Every PDF is 1,980 bytes smaller.** A host comparing documents byte for byte will see it; nothing drawn changes.
- **A page drawn or a file attached after `ToArray` or `Save` now throws `InvalidOperationException`.** It used to be
  left out of a file already made, in silence. Draw each document on a new `PdfBackend`.
- **The command line and the native library carry ZopfliSharp**, compiled in, under the Apache License 2.0: 244 KB
  more in the win-x64 library, 288 KB in the command line. Its licence and NOTICE travel in each archive under `licenses/zopflisharp/`, and
  `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` reproduces the NOTICE. The `Frisket`, `Frisket.Fonts` and `Frisket.Import` packages do not
  carry it and keep their licences.
